SCOPE. Solution mode is used rather than a single -p project because two
projects are owned and both must be mutated. Stryker mutates exactly the
projects referenced by the test projects listed below -- Provide.Telemetry
and Provide.Telemetry.OpenTelemetry. The probes, examples and consumer
smoke projects are in the solution but no test project references them, so
they are never mutated and need no exclusion entry.

THRESHOLD. break is 78, deliberately below the 79.41 % measured, not at
100. A threshold above the real score is a gate that fails on green and
gets disabled; the ~1.4pp of slack (about 23 mutants) absorbs the 10
timeout-classified mutants in ResilienceExecutor/Atomics, whose
classification depends on host load and would otherwise flip the gate on a
busy runner. Ratchet break upward as survivors are killed, never down.
RAISING IT. The survivors are dominated by missing assertions, not by
defects: default-value string literals on DTO properties (Types.cs,
Config.cs), env-var name literals whose lookups are only exercised through
their defaults (ConfigEnv.cs), per-signal OTLP path and log-level literals
(OpenTelemetryBackend.cs), and the SLO metric names (Governance.cs). Two
systematic classes are equivalent mutants that no test can kill:
ConfigureAwait(false) -> (true), which is a no-op without a synchronization
context, and comparisons whose two sides agree on every reachable value.
The circuit breaker's half-open block is the largest genuinely uncovered
region (10 no-coverage mutants in Resilience.cs) and needs an injectable
clock to reach, the same blocker the coverage floor in ci-csharp.yml
records. Roughly: asserting the literal-valued surfaces would move this
past 90; the breaker needs a design change first.
